title: Seatbelt & Rollover Protection (ROPS)
summary: Why the seatbelt is the single most effective protection in a rollover or sudden stop.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: ROPS only protects you if you stay inside the protective zone. Without a belt, operators can be thrown from the cab and crushed by the machine they were operating.

sections.heading: Correct use
sections.body: Fasten before starting the engine. Belt low across the hips, snug, not twisted. Inspect for fraying and buckle function at every pre-start check.

sections.heading: Common excuses
sections.body: 'I am only moving it a few metres' - most rollovers happen during short repositioning moves on slopes and soft ground.

quiz.q: When should the seatbelt be fastened?

options: You remain belted inside the cab

title: Hazard Zones & Ground Personnel Awareness
summary: Swing radius, blind spots, and communication protocols with ground crew.

sections.heading: Swing radius
sections.body: Treat the full swing radius plus 1 m as an exclusion zone. Stop all motion when anyone enters it.

sections.heading: Blind spots
sections.body: Rear and right-rear are the largest blind spots on excavators and loaders. Use cameras and mirrors; sound the horn before moving.

sections.heading: Communication
sections.body: Establish eye contact or radio confirmation before any ground worker approaches. Lower the bucket and neutralise controls.

quiz.q: A person walks into the swing radius. What do you do first?

title: Fatigue Management for Operators
summary: Recognising micro-sleeps and what to do before they cause an incident.

sections.heading: Warning signs
sections.body: Heavy eyelids, frequent blinking, drifting attention, missing radio calls. Micro-sleeps last 1-10 seconds - long enough to travel 20 m.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.body: Park safely, lower attachments, notify your supervisor. Short breaks, hydration and cab ventilation help; caffeine only masks fatigue.

title: Fuel Efficiency & Idle Reduction
summary: Every idle hour burns fuel, adds engine hours and shortens service intervals.

sections.heading: The cost
sections.body: A mid-size excavator burns ~4 L/h at idle. One hour of idle a day across a 20-machine fleet is roughly 20,000 L a year.

sections.heading: Habits
sections.body: Shut down if waiting more than 5 minutes. Use auto-idle and engine idle shutdown features. Plan truck arrivals to reduce waiting.

quiz.q: Waiting for a truck for 8 minutes - best practice?

title: Efficient Load Cycles
summary: Positioning, swing angle and bucket fill technique to cut cycle time.

sections.heading: Positioning
sections.body: Keep the truck at a 30-45 degree swing angle. Every extra 15 degrees of swing adds ~1 s per cycle.

sections.heading: Bucket fill
sections.body: Curl the bucket smoothly while crowding. Full buckets on fewer passes beat fast partial buckets.
